attacks.claim: The embargo badge sets text color #ffffff on background var(--surface), which is #ffffff in the default light theme. The label is effectively invisible (about 1:1 contrast), failing WCAG 2.1 AA 1.4.3 and the stated release requirement.
The unpublish control is a non-focusable <span> with only an onClick handler. Keyboard-only editors cannot reach or activate it (WCAG 2.1.1), and it exposes no role for assistive tech (4.1.2).
The unpublish control is icon-only with the icon aria-hidden and no aria-label, title, or visually hidden text, so screen-reader users get no name for a destructive action (4.1.2).
attacks.evidence: <TrashIcon aria-hidden="true" /> with ABSENT aria-label or visually hidden text on the wrapping span

attacks.claim: The unpublish control has only a :hover style and no :focus-visible rule, so keyboard focus is invisible (2.4.7).
attacks.evidence: .unpublish:hover { color: var(--danger); background: var(--surface-hover); } ABSENT: :focus-visible rule

attacks.claim: Unpublish is shown to every user who sees a published row, and the diff shows no authorization check on the onUnpublish path. The confirm dialog is client-side UX only and does not enforce permission. Server-side authorization is not shown in the artifact.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: server-side authz for onUnpublish; client shows {draft.status === "published" && (<span className={styles.unpublish} onClick={handleUnpublish}>

attacks.claim: handleUnpublish awaits onUnpublish with no try/catch and no error feedback. If the API call fails, the editor gets no indication the story is still live, which matters for a time-sensitive pull.
Unpublish changes a live story with a one-click entry point on every published row. The diff adds no audit record of actor and time and no undo, so an accidental confirm leaves no trail.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: audit/undo handling for onUnpublish; the confirm dialog is the only guard in handleUnpublish

attacks.claim: Embargo details, including lift times, are shown to all queue viewers with no role scoping, and the PR does not address whether other desks should see this.
The embargo label shows a time with no timezone indicator, even though the stated purpose is the newsroom timezone. Editors outside that zone can misread lift times.
attacks.evidence: formatInNewsroomTz(draft.embargoUntil!, "MMM d, HH:mm") with no zone label in the rendered text

attacks.claim: The unpublish handler has no pending state, so a double click can fire two unpublish requests while the confirm is resolving.
attacks.evidence: if (ok) await onUnpublish(draft.id); with no disabled or pending state

attacks.claim: DraftRow gains a required onUnpublish prop, but the diff does not update call sites. Other renderers will break or receive undefined.
attacks.evidence: onUnpublish: (id: string) => Promise<void>; added to Props with no change to the queue parent in the diff

attacks.claim: React.MouseEvent is used without importing React, which compiles only if a global React namespace is configured, and the diff does not show one.
attacks.evidence: async function handleUnpublish(e: React.MouseEvent) with imports that do not include React
